sections.what_happened: Araghchi (FT op-ed): 'Iran is prepared to give diplomacy another chance if we see strong evidence of a sincere desire on the part of the US to achieve a just and honourable solution to permanently end this conflict.' Demands: US lifts naval blockade, ends economic pressure, returns to the June Islamabad MoU (lift blockade, release frozen oil funds, remove sanctions) — sequencing deadlock persists: Washington wants Iran's nuclear program addressed first. Ghalibaf (NourNews, relayed by Reuters): Hormuz stays closed until the seven Islamabad-MoU conditions are met; US conveyed proposals via an intermediary but Tehran's position is 'clear and firm'; Qatar facilitating. Uranium red line via Munir: 'not a gram' of enriched uranium will leave Iran (BusinessToday, Oct 22). CENTCOM (X): blockade reached 100 days, prevented at least $25B in Iranian crude exports; no maritime exports/imports apart from humanitarian aid. Iran's armed forces chief: vowed a 'crushing and decisive response' to the enemy.
sections.what_verified: Economic Times, Times Now, arabnews.pk converge on the MoU/seven-conditions/diplomacy framing; Gulf News liveblog on the evening X posts; klse/Reuters chains on the Islamabad MoU history
sections.what_disputed: US has not confirmed it accepts the MoU terms or the 'seven conditions'; Trump's Truth Social accuses Iran of 'fake hits' and of driving oil prices up before midterms; Trump says nothing happens before the Nov 3 midterms; no confirmed US response to the seven-day plan
sections.why_matters: Diplomacy's last receipts: Araghchi's 'just and honourable solution' line against the 'not a gram of uranium' red line and CENTCOM's 100-day $25B ledger. Is this the on-ramp to the deal — or the script for the post-midterm war? The number to watch is zero: zero grams of uranium leaving Iran.
